stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: On La Gomera, one of the Canary Islands, residents once called to one another across steep ravines using Silbo Gomero, a form of Spanish rendered entirely in whistles. Linguist Rosa Medina argues that the system, far from being a simple code of signals, preserves something more fundamental than individual words______ the stress patterns and vowel contrasts of spoken Spanish, translated into shifts of pitch.
choices: words, they are the stress patterns
explanation: Start by crossing out the interrupter "far from being a simple code of signals." What remains, "Linguist Rosa Medina argues that the system preserves something more fundamental than individual words," is a complete sentence. It also points forward, because it promises to name that "something." The text after the blank is only a noun phrase, and it names that thing. A colon is the mark that joins a complete sentence to a phrase that explains it.

B.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon needs a complete sentence on both sides, and "the stress patterns and vowel contrasts of spoken Spanish, translated into shifts of pitch" has no main verb, so it is a fragment.

C.why: Adding "they are" turns the second part into a complete sentence. A bare comma then joins two complete sentences, which is a comma splice.

D.why: A period makes "The stress patterns and vowel contrasts of spoken Spanish, translated into shifts of pitch" stand alone as a sentence. It has no main verb, so it is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: The tiger pistol shrimp spends much of its life digging burrows in sandy seafloors, but its eyesight is so poor that it cannot detect approaching predators. It therefore shares its burrow with a goby, and the partnership, which can last for the lifetimes of both animals, depends on a simple trade______ the goby's vigilance in exchange for the shrimp's shelter. The shrimp keeps one antenna on the fish at all times and retreats the instant the goby flicks its tail.
choices: trade, it is the goby's vigilance
explanation: Ignore the interrupter "which can last for the lifetimes of both animals." The clause "the partnership depends on a simple trade" is complete, and it promises to say what the trade is. The text after the blank is a noun phrase that names the trade. A colon introduces exactly this kind of explanation.

A.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon must have a complete sentence on each side, but "the goby's vigilance in exchange for the shrimp's shelter" has no verb.

B.why: "It is the goby's vigilance..." is a complete sentence. Joining it to the earlier complete clause with only a comma creates a comma splice.

D.why: A period leaves "The goby's vigilance in exchange for the shrimp's shelter" on its own as a sentence. It has no verb, so it is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: When the interstellar object 'Oumuamua passed through the inner solar system in 2017, astronomers quickly calculated its trajectory. As observations accumulated, however, the object displayed one behavior that gravity alone could not account for______ a small but measurable acceleration away from the Sun. Comets often accelerate this way because escaping gas pushes on them, yet telescopes detected no gas or dust around 'Oumuamua.
choices: for, this was a small but measurable
explanation: "The object displayed one behavior that gravity alone could not account for" is a complete sentence, even though it ends with a preposition. It also announces that one behavior is about to be named. What follows the blank is a noun phrase that names it. A colon is correct here.

A.why: A period turns "A small but measurable acceleration away from the Sun" into its own sentence. It has no verb, so it is a fragment.

C.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. A semicolon needs a complete sentence after it, and here the second part is only a noun phrase.

D.why: "This was a small but measurable acceleration..." is a complete sentence. Joining it to the first complete sentence with a bare comma creates a comma splice.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Clark's nutcrackers, which inhabit the high-elevation pine forests of western North America, bury tens of thousands of seeds each autumn in widely scattered caches. To survive the winter, the birds depend on an ability that researchers have tested repeatedly in laboratory aviaries______ a spatial memory precise enough to relocate many of those caches months later, often beneath a layer of snow.
choices: aviaries, it is a spatial memory
explanation: The relative clause "that researchers have tested repeatedly in laboratory aviaries" makes the first part long, but "the birds depend on an ability" is still a complete sentence. It also leaves the ability unnamed. The text after the blank is a noun phrase that names it, so the colon is the right mark.

A.why: Adding "it is" makes the second part a complete sentence. Two complete sentences joined only by a comma form a comma splice.

B.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. "A spatial memory precise enough to relocate..." has no main verb, so it cannot stand on the far side of a semicolon.

C.why: A period makes "A spatial memory precise enough to relocate many of those caches months later" a sentence by itself. It has no main verb, so it is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Fossil leaves of Glossopteris, a seed-bearing plant that flourished roughly 270 million years ago, have been found in South America, Africa, India, Antarctica, and Australia. Because the plant's heavy seeds could not have drifted across oceans, the fossils' distribution supported an idea that many early twentieth-century geologists rejected______ the proposal that these landmasses were once joined in a single continent.
explanation: Set aside the introductory "Because..." clause. The main clause, "the fossils' distribution supported an idea that many early twentieth-century geologists rejected," is complete, and it points ahead to an idea it has not yet named. "The proposal that these landmasses were once joined" is a noun phrase that identifies the idea. A colon is the correct way to join them.

B.why: "It was the proposal..." is a complete sentence. Joining it to the preceding complete sentence with only a comma creates a comma splice.

C.why: You chose the semicolon because it looks formal. The text after it, "the proposal that these landmasses were once joined," is a noun phrase, so this is not a complete sentence. The verb "were joined" belongs to the "that" clause, not to the phrase as a whole.

D.why: A period leaves "The proposal that these landmasses were once joined in a single continent" as a fragment. The only verb is inside the "that" clause, so the phrase has no main verb.
